typography.usage: Native Title, Heading1 and JournalOpening use Baskerville for reflective openings.
Native Normal paragraphs use Baskerville 13 pt for sustained reflection.
Heading2, JournalLabel, metadata and links use Noto Sans for the record layer.

recognitionRules: Use Baskerville for reflective titles and reading paragraphs; reserve Noto Sans for record headings, metadata and links.
Keep the observation concrete before introducing an explanation.
Give the attempted change and its result separate passages.
Leave room for an image or sketch with a factual caption.

principles: Let a concrete image or material action carry the opening; explain the work plainly afterward.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Notice the small thing that keeps returning. Try a change you can describe.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid abstract manifestos that displace the actual work.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Begin with one thing you can make or inspect.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use A QUIETER PRACTICE in Baskerville with a short light rule below the name. No leaf or mindfulness symbol.
invariants: Use Baskerville for reflective titles and reading paragraphs; reserve Noto Sans for record headings, metadata and links.
Keep the observation concrete before introducing an explanation.
Give the attempted change and its result separate passages.
adaptations: A daily note may use only observation, change and reflection.
A project review can gather several dated entries without rewriting their uncertainty.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
